newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung sets 97 telecom sales at $4.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Samsung sets 97 telecom sales at $4.2 bln.

text.p: Samsung Electronics Co, a unit of Samsung Group, said its telecommunications business division targeted sales of $4.2 billion in 1997.
Sales figures for 1996 were not immediately available.
The company said in a statement that it would boost its investment in the telecommunications sector by 27 percent over last year to $715 million.
Samsung said the investment would break down to $264 million for new facilities and $451 million in research and development.
Samsung said existing business areas would be restructured to maximise profitability.
"Businesses with limited profit-making potential will be phased out," it said in a statement.
The company added that overseas sales were expected to rise to 26 percent of total sales and further increase to 55 percent by the year 2000. Last year, overseas sales amounted to just 20 percent.
Products in high-growth areas, such as printers and key phones, will be fully supported, it said.
Samsung said it planned to establish strategic alliances with leading overseas companies to strengthen international competitiveness.
